## Dropped after hand-checking (a source disagrees; better absent than wrong)

- NGC4303: the only post-2016 value (24.2 Mpc, 2018ApJ...861...49H) is 40% above every other measurement (10.6-19.8 Mpc)
- NGC6994: M73 is an asterism of four stars, not a cluster, so it has no single distance
- NGC40: modern Gaia values 1.8-2.0 kpc against 1.1-1.2 kpc in the older papers; the sources disagree by a factor 1.7
- NGC6729: proxy R CrA cloud has a single value (R19)
- C99: proxy Coalsack has a single value (R19)
- IC4592: only a single nu Sco value, which contradicts IC4601 in the same complex (R19)
- LDN1147: proxy LDN 1228 has a single value (R19)
- LDN1235: proxy LDN 1228 has a single value (R19)
- NYCEP: a star's distance for a nebula field; single value (R19)
- ZETOPH: a star's distance for a nebula field (R19)
- AFLAC: a star's distance for a nebula field; single value (R19)
- NGC2246: single SIMBAD value 2.4 kpc (2006ApJ...653.1226Q) disagrees with the Rosette's ~1.5 kpc
- NGC6537: single SIMBAD value 3.8 kpc (2010ApJ...714.1096S); published Red Spider distances range 1-4 kpc
- NGC6905: the only modern value (Gaia, 2.7 kpc) is 50% above the older 1.75 kpc values; sources disagree

## Hand-check notes (written by hand; the script keeps only the part above regenerated, so re-add this after a rebuild)

- Brief test values: M45 439 ly (444 expected), M31 2.53 Mly, M8 4149 ly (SIMBAD has one value, Zucker et al. 2020, 1272 pc),
  NGC7331 47.3 Mly. NGC7293 (Helix): the plain median (152-201 pc) was 522 ly, 20% under the Gaia value; replaced by the Gaia
  DR2/EDR3 pair (about 653 ly).
- Round 1 claim that every galaxy and nebula was within 20% was an overclaim; see Round 2 notes for what was actually checked.
   Large spreads (M32, M33, M110, M64, M95) come from a few erroneous SIMBAD rows; the medians are fine.
- Single-value rows (n=1) for old globulars, M8, Crab, Cave, Carina are sensible; globulars were cross-checked against Baumgardt & Vasiliev (2021) and the two
  that were more than 15% off (M10, M30) use their values.
- Proxies (parent cloud, cluster or illuminating star) are listed above with the reason. They are about right (tens of percent)
  but are the weakest rows: IC434/B33 (sigma Ori cluster), IC4592 (nu Sco), IC4601 (HD 147889), LDN1147/LDN1235 (Cepheus Flare via LDN 1228).
- NGC6992/NGC6960 (Veil): one literature value for the whole Cygnus Loop; the doi was found through Crossref, the 725 +/- 15 pc figure is from its abstract.
- Left out on purpose: no SIMBAD value and no source we can cite (nebulae like NGC2024/M78/IC2177/IC1318, B142, the Coathanger, M24, M40).

## Round 2 notes (R19: modern-era medians)

- Rule: median of measurements published 2016 or later when at least one exists, else of all; `n` counts what was used. For galaxies,
  kpc-scale rows (Gaia matching a foreground star) are discarded first. Proxy rows need n >= 2 and a physical association.
- Checked by hand against published values: M27 1,248 ly (n=2); M104 31.1 Mly; M88 54.5 Mly; NGC3132 2,645 ly; NGC6543 4,455 ly (n=1, Gaia
  2020yCat.1350....0G); NGC7635 8,969 ly (n=2); NGC4038 72.0 Mly (n=1, 22.08 Mpc, 2016AJ....152...50T; Antennae TRGB value).
- NGC6302 2,425 ly (n=2, 741/746 pc, 2008ApJ...689..194S, 2010ApJ...714.1096S): about 29% under the ~3,400 ly usually quoted; kept as the only SIMBAD
  measurements, but the weakest planetary row.
- NGC3561 (the Guitar, Arp 105) 412 Mly, n=1: 126.4 Mpc (2007ApJ...655..790C), consistent with its redshift distance; kept.
- NGC2573 now the median of four 25-30 Mpc values (Gaia stellar matches removed), about 90 Mly.
- Dropped: NGC40, NGC6905, NGC4303 (sources disagree), M73, ZETOPH, AFLAC, NYCEP, IC4592, LDN1147, LDN1235, C99, NGC6729 (see above).
- What was NOT checked: most other rows were only compared with remembered published values, with no independent second source.
